To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the shock wave front smearing is caused by the fast dissociation at the front; 2) the dissociation front is ahead of the shock front and moves at a higher velocity; 3) the smearing is more pronounced at high impact velocities and for low-Z materials.
the dissociation smears the shock front in liquid deuterius, and that this effect is important at impact velocities of about 1 km/s and above.
the shock wave front in liquid deuterius is smeared at high impact velocities, and that this effect is due to the dissociation of molecules at the front.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the shock wave propagation in low-Z dissociating liquids.

the study of shock waves in low-Z materials, in particular, liquid hydrogen and deuterium, which are of interest for astrophysics, planetary sciences, inertial confinement fusion and shock compression of hydrogen-rich materials.
the study of shock wave propagation and material response to extreme dynamic loading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the experimental results on the shock wave propagation in low Z liquids are not yet fully understood and that further theoretical and experimental work is needed to clarify the issue.
the Hugoniot data for deuterium, as well as for hydrogen, can be described by a simple equation of state, which is based on the dissociation of molecules and is independent of the impact velocity.
shock wave propagation in low-Z liquids can be well described by molecular dynamics simulations, if the dissociation process is properly taken into account.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dissociation is the main factor that controls the Hugoniot curve of liquid deuterium.
the shock wave front is not a single point but it is a region with a finite width, the width of which depends on the impact velocity and the dissociation energy of the molecules.
shock wave propagation in dissociable liquids is not a simple process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the smearing of shock wave in dissociating low- Z liquid is a universal phenomenon and it is not related to the specific features of the liquid deuterium.
the smearing of the front is an important effect which has to be taken into account in the analysis of shock wave propagation and Hugoniots in low-Z liquids.
the shock wave in liquid deuterius propagates as a single phase, and the observed two phase region is an artifact of the experimental technique.
